items.q: What should you remember about **Three-tier diagnostic**?
items.a: **voice + body + words determine** rookie / pretty good / natural; use it to self-locate before practicing.

items.q: What should you remember about **Unconscious incompetence**?
items.a: **most people are rookies** because they don't know what they're doing wrong.

items.q: What should you remember about **Rookie voice**?
items.a: **flat delivery (one speed/pitch/volume/emotion);** vocal fry; filler words every breath → unsure, unclear, unconfident.

items.q: What should you remember about **Brilliant ≠ great communicator**?
items.a: **Zuckerberg/Musk/Altman can succeed without polish; mere mortals cannot.**

items.q: What should you remember about **Rookie body**?
items.a: **no expression, bad posture,** awkward eye contact; behaviors are changeable habits.

items.q: What should you remember about **Rookie words**?
items.a: **no structure, circles, winging** it; listener does all cognitive work.

items.q: What should you remember about **Self-awareness exercise**?
items.a: **record 2-min answer to** "Why improve communication?"; transcribe (Gemini); audit fillers, clarity, repetition.

items.q: What should you remember about **Range scale**?
items.a: **rookies use a sliver; pretty-good** uses more but stays in the middle; naturals use full range.

items.q: What should you remember about **Play at the edges**?
items.a: **Alex Hormozi with Tony Robbins vs Diary of a CEO**: same person, more range = "version I've never seen.".

items.q: What should you remember about **Fear of judgment trap**?
items.a: **keeps pretty-good speakers safe; spotlight effect rebuttal**: people think about themselves, not you.

items.q: What should you remember about **Only move with purpose**?
items.a: **Mark Manson stage pacing** as non functional body language; stillness is a pro tool.

items.q: What should you remember about **Frameworks as filters**?
items.a: **PREP, STAR, 321, PARA, PEEL** distill thinking so listeners don't follow your raw thought process.
